headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill mandates large energy users, such as data centers, to bear the costs of grid infrastructure upgrades necessitated by their high electricity demand, rather than socializing these costs across all ratepayers.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Governor Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users.
news_headline: Spanberger Says Data Centers Should Pay Own Power Bill
news_summary: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger is advocating for data centers to bear the costs of new transmission infrastructure, a stance supported by a recent State Corporation Commission decision. This move aims to prevent hundreds of millions of dollars in transmission costs from being passed on to residential and small-business customers.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates local water authorities to publicly report the monthly water usage of data centers, increasing transparency and providing data for future water resource management.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Virginia Law Requires Data Center Water Usage Public
news_summary: A new Virginia law, effective January 1, 2027, requires local water authorities to report data center water usage to the Department of Environmental Quality, making the numbers publicly accessible. This legislation aims to provide credible data for public discourse on data center water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for noise and other environmental impacts for new high energy use facilities, empowering localities to consider community concerns regarding data center development.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents, community groups, environmental advocates, Governor Spanberger's administration.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate industry.
news_headline: Roanoke Delegate Helped Write Virginia's New Data Center Law
news_summary: Virginia's new law, effective July 1, 2026, requires developers of large data centers to conduct site assessments examining noise profiles on nearby residential areas and schools. While it mandates studies, the law does not set specific noise limits or water caps, leaving some regulatory power to localities.
